Integration Boost and Distribution Reward stack on the same
Two Integration Boost Instances inherit their near-term qual

title: Integration Boost makes the target chain a first-class governed parameter, spanning Base and Ethereum Mainnet
content:
Each Integration Boost Instance carries an explicit Integration Partner Chain parameter: Euler is "on Base blockchain" (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.1.1.3), Curve and Morpho are "on Ethereum Mainnet blockchain" (.2.1.3, .3.1.3), and the prospective Compound Instance is on Base (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.4.1.2.3). Reward addresses are recorded per Instance and, for Euler and Compound, are annotated with the chain they live on.

This is a different treatment from the Distribution Reward primitive, where the chain appears only implicitly through the choice of Tracking Methodology ("Ethereum Mainnet General", "Base Tracking"). Here the chain is its own named parameter with its own document.

The distinction fits the two instruments. A frontend's users can transact anywhere, so the chain is a property of the measurement; a lending market or AMM pool is deployed at a specific address on a specific chain, so the chain is a property of the relationship itself. Making it explicit means an integration cannot silently migrate chains without an Artifact edit, and the reward address cannot be misread as belonging to the wrong network.

Strategically, the split across Base and Mainnet shows Skybase's demand-side spending is already multi-chain, with the two newest Instances — Euler and the prospective Compound — both on Base rather than Mainnet.
description: Euler and Compound boosts run on Base while Curve and Morpho run on Ethereum Mainnet, each with its own reward address — unlike Distribution Rewards where the chain is implied by the tracking method.
